answer: Convex reputation weighting makes splitting an identity a losing move: voting weight is reputation squared, so spreading reputation R over n identities yields n*(R/n)^2 = R^2/n, only a tenth of the weight for ten fakes. Every new account starts at zero in the public atlas and earns reputation only by passing audited tasks, so a lotus of fresh accounts has almost no vote. Reputation is non-transferable, so many thin shale layers of fakes never stack into real weight.
